In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reaction of cysteinyl peptides and thiol compounds with thioesters in aqueous medium is governed primarily by the concentration of the sulfhydryl anion.
the thiol pK (a) is the most relevant parameter in determining the reactivity of the sulfhydryl groups in peptides with thioesters.
the reaction of cysteinyl peptides and proteins with palmitoylation substrates is governed mainly by the concentration of thiolate anions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reaction of a cysteinyl peptide with a thioester is determined by the thiolate ionization constant, which in turn is influenced by the amino acid composition of the peptide.
the reactivity of cysteine residues towards thioesters in aqueous solution is mainly determined by the pK(a) of the attacking sulfide.
the thiol pK is the most important factor influencing the rate and specificity of non-enzyme-mediated palmitoylation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reactivity of a given thiol is determined by the acid-base properties, which can be modulated by the local microenvironment.
the reactivity of the cysteines in peptides and proteins is mainly determined by the pK(a) of their sulfhydryl groups, which in turn is strongly affected by the local environment.
the reactivity of cysteine residues in peptides is mainly determined by the acid-base properties and not by the steric hindrance of the thiol.
